label: final copy step of length-3 sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase. About 80% of activation mass sits at step 5 of L=3 sequences, the last output step: the input there is orig(1) and the model outputs orig(2). It is active on roughly 77% of those steps, and this predicate covers 96% of the top activation quartile. Strongest when the input there is j (top examples are like w j t <DEL> w [j]). Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, or on the first occurrence of a token. The remaining ~20% of mass is weak scattered firing at later copy steps of longer sequences (mostly the last or second-to-last output, with j input overrepresented), which no simple clause captures without losing precision.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: j, r, o, l, g, n; least: 1, y, b, a) and the first original token (most: n, 2, c, l, g, y; least: f, s, i, m); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, L=3, t=5.
